message.content: We prove the problem is NP-Complete. First, we show that the problem is in NP. A certificate simply lists chosen vertices and edges, checked in polynomial time. Next we must establish the hardness direction by reducing from the classic NP-Complete problem SUBSET-SUM. Given an instance with elements a1 through an and target k, build a graph of n isolated vertices. For each element ai, create one isolated vertex vi with weight ai, and place no edges anywhere in the entire graph. Because there are no edges, any subgraph is simply a subset of vertices, and its total weight is the sum of those vertex weights. Thus, the constructed graph contains a subgraph of total weight k if and only if some subset of the original elements sums to exactly the target k. Since SUBSET-SUM is already known to be NP-Complete and this reduction clearly runs in polynomial time, we conclude that SUBGRAPH-WEIGHT is NP-hard, and with NP membership shown, it is NP-Complete.
